name: Cloak
summary: The unit turns invisible to the enemy: it cannot be seen or picked as a target, yet it stays solid and area damage still lands on it. Versions differ in when it hides: while standing still, at all times until it attacks, while no enemy is close, or on a key that runs on a timer or an energy meter. Most show themselves for a moment when they fire, use an ability or are hit, then fade back a few seconds later; a few keep the cloak while they attack. Detectors, scans and enemies who come very close uncover it for their whole team. Unlike disguise it is not seen at all, unlike the stealth sensor trait it is fully hidden rather than hard to spot, and unlike shroud-area it hides the unit, not the ground around it.
counterplay: Bring a detector: a unit, turret or building that uncovers cloaked enemies near it for the whole team, such as the Sentry Drone and Listening Outpost in Generals, the Pitbull in Tiberium Wars, the Vimana in Tempest Rising or the Nightingale in Halo Wars 2.
Scan the area: a reveal on a key or an item shows cloaked units there for a few seconds (StarCraft II's scanner sweep, Warcraft III's Dust of Appearance).
Fire into the area: splash, area spells and mines hit cloaked units although nobody can target them (StarCraft II's Psionic Storm and EMP round, Dota 2's area spells).
Watch for tells: the shimmer of a moving cloak, footprints or dust, the flicker when it is hit or bumps into someone, and the sound of cloaking and uncloaking.
Punish the reveal: nearly every cloak drops when the unit attacks, so return fire at once; in Generals idle units nearby attack a revealed unit by themselves.
Get close: many versions are seen by any enemy within a short distance (Brawl Stars' Leon, Iron Harvest's Olga, infantry near a hidden unit in Tempest Rising).
Drain its resource: a cloak that runs on energy ends when the energy does, and draining it (Warcraft III's Arcane Tower against the Blademaster) limits how often it is used.

other_examples.note: A fast, fragile missile tank that stays invisible until it fires; its generator brings the cloak back almost at once after each volley, so it hits and fades again. Units with suitable sensors, the Pitbull among them, find it at close range, and rocket infantry and heavy armour that survive a volley punish it. Players use it to scout and to raid aircraft and vehicles.

sources.note: Says most stealth units across the series lose it when they attack or come under fire, and that detectors are units, buildings or abilities.

other_examples.note: An unarmed support vehicle that deploys to cloak friendly units around it and spots other cloaked units. It cannot move while the field is up, so players bring at least two and leapfrog, moving the force from one field to the next while it stays hidden; the bubble may flicker when the generator is hit.

Stealth, Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Lists it under Tiberian Sun as cloaking nearby friendly units and buildings and detecting cloaked ones.

other_examples.note: A researched toggle that costs energy to start and keeps draining it; the unit can move, attack and, for the Ghost, cast while cloaked, and the cloak ends when the energy runs out. Only a player with a detector can target it, though attentive players see a distortion, and area effects such as Psionic Storm, EMP rounds and Fungal Growth still hit it. Cloaked Banshees force the opponent to invest in detection or scans early.

other_examples.unit: Stealth profiles (Drone Mauler, Scrambler, Commando, Condor, Sniper and others)
other_examples.note: The game sorts hiding into four kinds: while still and not attacking, while not attacking even on the move, for a time on a button, or on a toggle that attacking switches off. A hidden unit is invisible except to detector units and buildings (the Vimana is one) and to infantry close by, and its owner sees it flashing and translucent.

other_examples.unit: Active camouflage (UNSC Sniper, Elite Honor Guard, Shroud, cloaking generator)
other_examples.note: Some units cloak themselves, the Shroud and the cloaking generator cloak nearby units or buildings in an area, and two leaders have powers that cloak units for a while. Nobody can target a cloaked unit until a detecting unit (the Nightingale aircraft, the Engineers) uncovers it.

The hero turns invisible and faster for a time and can pass through units. Attacking ends it, but that first blow deals bonus damage, and the cooldown starts only when it breaks. Players use it to escape, to scout enemy towns and to open fights; the answers are detection (sentry wards, flying machines, Dust of Appearance) and draining the hero's mana.

shooter_analogues.note: A power-up, a piece of equipment or an armour ability that leaves the player as a faint shimmer. Shooting, grenades, melee and using equipment break or weaken it, and taking damage makes the user fade in. In Reach it is almost perfect while standing still and much weaker when moving fast, and it also scrambles the motion trackers of the user and of nearby enemies, which warns them, and dulls the user's hearing. In Infinite it is carried until used, and a carrier who dies before using it drops it for anyone to pick up.

Alt-fire turns the Spy fully invisible after a short fade. He cannot attack while cloaked and must wait until he has fully reappeared before he can. Taking damage or bumping into an enemy makes him flicker into view, cloaking and uncloaking make a whoosh, and a meter limits how long he stays hidden; ammo pickups and dispensers refill it. Teammates see a faint silhouette, and he takes a little less damage while cloaked.

sources.title: Invisibility Watch, Official Team Fortress Wiki

shooter_analogues.unit: Leon's Smoke Bomb, Lollipop Drop and Limbo
shooter_analogues.note: In this top-down team shooter, Leon's super hides him for a few seconds. Attacking ends it, taking damage or picking up items shows him for a moment, and enemies within a short distance can see him, a limit added soon after release; enemy minions cannot find him at all. A gadget drops a lollipop that hides him and nearby teammates until it decays or is destroyed, a star power speeds him up while hidden, and his hypercharge lets him attack without breaking it.

In this top-down game an invisible unit vanishes from enemy screens and minimaps and cannot be selected or attacked, though most area spells still hit it. Most sources break when the unit reaches the point of an attack or a cast; some come back on their own after a delay, and many have a short fade before they start. Allies see it as transparent, and True Sight from towers, other buildings and some abilities cancels it.

player_translation.summary: A player who can vanish from enemy screens, minimaps and auto-aim and so choose where a fight starts. Its own attacks break the cloak, so the skill is picking the moment; enemies answer with detectors, scans, area fire and an eye for a close-range shimmer.
as_user: Press Q, or stand still, or simply keep away from enemies, depending on the variant, and fade out over about a second. While hidden you cannot be targeted, your name tag and minimap marker disappear for enemies, and turrets and bots ignore you.
You stay solid: you cannot walk through enemies, and splash, mines and area effects hurt you as usual.
Firing or using an ability drops the cloak at once, so the first shot is also your reveal; the cloak returns a couple of seconds after your last attack, or when the key is ready again.
A cloak on a key runs on a meter or a timer; the passive versions cost nothing but have limits (only while still, or only while no enemy is near).

A detector or scan uncovers you for the whole enemy team with a loud cue, so you learn where they stand and route around them. Cloaked units are usually fragile: once seen, retreat or finish the job fast.
as_target: A cloaked enemy shows only as a faint shimmer when it moves within a short distance of you, and as a ripple when it is hit; further away nothing shows.
You cannot lock on to it, but you can fire at the shimmer: explosives, area attacks and mines hit it anyway.
Its first shot gives it away: the reveal cue (a sound and a flash where it stands) tells you where to fire back.
Ping the shimmer or the reveal; a teammate's detector or scan uncovers it for everyone.
teammates: The cloaked player scouts and pings what is coming (spotter), or waits in ambush for enemies the team lures in.
The other team escorts its detectors and saves scans for pushes; a cloak-heavy team forces a detector pick.
With the cloak-field variant a whole squad stays hidden until it opens fire, so teammates must hold their fire and move together.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse fires, and firing breaks the cloak.
Q (signature or extra): cloak, fading out over about a second; Q again drops it early. One counted key.
Passive variants use no key: stand still, or keep out of enemies' reach, and the cloak comes back by itself.
Cloak-field variant: E deploys or packs up the field device, which cloaks allies in its radius while it runs.
feedback: The cloaked player sees their unit as a translucent outline, a cloak meter and a 'detected' warning when a detector or scan uncovers them.
Teammates see a translucent silhouette and the usual minimap marker, so nobody walks into a hidden friend's line of fire.
Enemies see a faint distortion only within a short radius, plus footprints or dust on soft ground; cloaking and uncloaking play a distinct sound and a shimmer burst that reads from above.
Detector range is drawn as a ring for its own team, and an uncovered unit gets a red outline and a minimap marker for the whole team while it stays in range.
changes_from_rts: RTS cloaks hide a unit completely from anyone without a detector. Against human players a shooter needs honest tells (a shimmer up close, sound, footprints), or being shot by nothing feels unfair.
RTS stealth works by stopping target selection; in a shooter players aim by hand, so splash, area attacks and mines must still hurt a cloaked unit, as StarCraft II and Dota 2 allow.
Generals and Tiberium Wars units hide again almost at once after firing. In a shooter that lets a sniper fire, vanish and fire again, so each attack reveals the shooter for a couple of seconds.
RTS detectors are separate units; here detection must be easy to field (a sensor trait, a scan key, a turret), or one cloaked player dominates a match.
The Generals rule that idle enemies hunt a revealed unit becomes a team-wide marker: once revealed, the whole enemy team sees it for a moment.

team_play.notes: A cloaked player mostly scouts, picks off stragglers or opens fights; the cloak-field variant hides a whole push, which raises team play. The other team needs a detector, a scan or area fire, and players who call out a shimmer.

notes: The server must not send a cloaked enemy's position to clients that cannot see it, or a modified client becomes a wallhack; the close-range shimmer is decided on the server.
Every automatic targeting system (turrets, bots, aim assist, lock-ons) must skip cloaked units unless a detector or scan uncovers them.
A clear state machine per variant: fade-out, fade-in, reveal on attack, reveal on damage and the re-cloak delay.
A shimmer effect that reads from a top-down camera on every map, plus footprints or dust on soft ground.
The hidden-state and detection system is shared with burrow, disguise, the stealth and detector sensor traits and reveal-area, so it is built once.
Whoever attacks first from cloak wins most fights; keep cloaked units fragile, make the first shot reveal the shooter, and add a re-cloak delay.
A cloak combined with a burst weapon or a self-destruct can delete key players with no warning, so detectors must be cheap and common.
A free passive cloak lets one player hold a spot all match, as a parked Sentry Drone does; limit it to standing still, or let scans and close enemies break it.
A cloaked player capturing an objective or carrying a flag unseen would decide matches; capturing should reveal them.
From above, a shimmer is easy to miss on busy maps; the tell needs one consistent look and sound.
Teammates need a clear translucent silhouette to know where a cloaked friend is.
Spectators, replays and kill cams should always show cloaked units with an outline.

variants.name: Cloak on a key
variants.summary: Press to fade out; the cloak lasts until a timer or an energy meter runs out, or until you attack. The default.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Ghost and Banshee, Team Fortress 2 Invisibility Watch, Brawl Stars Leon, Halo active camouflage, Warcraft III Wind Walk, Tempest Rising Condor and Sniper

variants.name: Hide when still
variants.summary: Passive: hidden whenever you neither move nor attack; moving or firing shows you, and you vanish again a moment after you stop.
variants.seen_in: Generals Sentry Drone, Tempest Rising Drone Mauler and Scrambler

variants.name: Hidden until you attack
variants.summary: Passive: hidden at all times, on the move too, except for a couple of seconds after each attack.
variants.seen_in: Generals Jarmen Kell, Tiberium Wars Stealth Tank, Tempest Rising Commando

variants.name: Hidden at a distance
variants.summary: Passive: hidden while no enemy is close; an enemy that comes within a short range sees you, and any action gives you away until the enemies are gone again.
variants.seen_in: Iron Harvest Olga Morozova; Brawl Stars Leon, whom nearby enemies see

variants.name: Ambush strike
variants.summary: While cloaked you move faster and pass through units, and the attack that breaks the cloak deals bonus damage.
variants.seen_in: Warcraft III Blademaster Wind Walk; Brawl Stars Leon's speed and damage bonuses

variants.name: Cloak field
variants.summary: A deployed device or an anchored mode cloaks every ally in a radius; the carrier cannot move while it runs and the field flickers when hit, so two carriers leapfrog a force forward.
variants.seen_in: Tiberian Sun Firestorm Mobile Stealth Generator, Halo Wars 2 Shroud and cloaking generator, Brawl Stars Leon's Lollipop Drop

variants.name: Noisy cloak
variants.summary: Cloaking also scrambles the radar and minimap of you and every enemy near you and muffles your own hearing, which hides you better but tells them someone cloaked is close.

variants.name: Fire from cloak
variants.summary: The cloak holds while you attack, at a steep energy cost, so only detectors, scans and area fire can answer it.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Cloak on the Ghost and Banshee, Brawl Stars Leon's hypercharge

adds_strengths.why: Unseen and untargetable until it acts, so it scouts freely and chooses where and when a fight starts.

adds_weaknesses.why: Its own attacks, detectors, scans and enemies close by give it away, and a cloaked unit is usually fragile once seen.

counters.why: Automatic turrets and bots cannot fire at what they cannot see, so it walks past them unless they detect.
Slow artillery and siege units behind the line are easy prey for a unit that reaches them unseen, as cloaked Ghosts and Banshees show against tank-heavy armies.

countered_by.why: A detector uncovers it for the whole team, and once seen it is a fragile unit in the wrong place.
A scan over its position shows it for a few seconds.
Splash and area damage hit it without a target, so fire at a shimmer still lands.

open_questions: How much should a cloaked enemy show from a top-down camera: nothing beyond a short radius (the proposal here), or a faint shimmer at any range while it moves?
Must every attack break the cloak, as in Generals, Halo and Team Fortress 2, or may a rare high-tier variant fire from cloak as in StarCraft II?
Can a cloaked player capture objectives or carry a flag unseen? The proposal is that capturing reveals them.
Do passive cloaks (hide when still, hidden at a distance) count against a tier's passive budget like any other passive?
Should the Generals rule that idle units go after a revealed unit carry over as a short team-wide marker on every reveal?

shooter_fit.reason: Team Fortress 2, Halo, Brawl Stars and Dota 2 show invisibility working in team games, two of them top-down. It needs honest close-range tells, a reveal on attack and common detectors, or it frustrates the players who get ambushed.
